title: Monthly vs Yearly Subscription Cost: When Annual Saves
metaDescription: Convert monthly, quarterly and weekly plans to a yearly cost, see when a yearly plan saves money and when it becomes a trap, using clear rupee examples.
h1: Is a yearly subscription cheaper than paying monthly?
summary: To compare plans fairly, convert every price to a yearly figure: multiply a monthly price by 12, a quarterly price by 4 and a weekly price by 52. A yearly plan saves money only if you would keep the service for most of the year, because a monthly plan can cost less if you stop early, even though its headline price looks higher.
keywords: convert monthly subscription to yearly cost

sections.heading: How to annualise a subscription cost
paragraphs: The fair way to compare plans is to put them on the same yearly basis. Multiply a monthly price by 12. Multiply a quarterly price by 4. A weekly charge is multiplied by 52, not by 4 times 12, because a year has 52 weeks. To get an effective monthly cost from a yearly price, divide by 12.

Take an illustrative plan at ₹199 a month. The monthly plan costs ₹199 × 12 = ₹2,388 a year. A quarterly plan at ₹549 per quarter costs ₹549 × 4 = ₹2,196 a year. A yearly plan at ₹1,999 costs ₹1,999 a year, which is about ₹167 a month. These are example numbers, not a real plan's price, so check the current price on the plan page before you decide.
list: Weekly price × 52 = yearly cost (₹50 a week is ₹2,600 a year)

sections.heading: When a yearly plan saves money
paragraphs: In the example above, the yearly plan saves ₹2,388 − ₹1,999 = ₹389 a year, which is about 16 per cent. The quarterly plan saves ₹192 a year. A saving of this size is only worth having if you would really keep the service for the whole year.

The break-even point is what matters. Monthly costs ₹199 for each month you stay. Ten months on the monthly plan costs ₹1,990, which is ₹9 less than the yearly ₹1,999, so monthly is cheaper for any stay of up to 10 months. At 11 months the monthly plan costs ₹2,189, so the yearly plan wins once you expect to stay for 11 months or more.

sections.heading: When a yearly plan is a trap
paragraphs: The trap is the upfront charge. A yearly plan takes the full amount on the renewal date, so if you stop using the service in month 4, you have already paid for eight months you did not use. The yearly saving is only real if you use the service for the whole term.

Refunds are not guaranteed. Google's help page says that in some instances you may be eligible for a refund, but its own example of a one-year subscription cancelled halfway describes access continuing until the end of the paid year, not a refund of the unused months. Google also lists partial refunds for subscriptions as a region-specific policy for Israel, France and Germany, so do not assume a pro-rated refund on an Indian yearly plan. For an app's own refund terms, contact the developer.
Check the price again at every renewal. A yearly plan you bought at one price may renew at a different price, so the saving you were promised may not hold the next year.

sections.heading: What cancelling does on each store
paragraphs: On Android, open subscriptions in Google Play, select the subscription and tap Cancel subscription. Google says you can keep using the subscription for the time you have already paid, and it warns that uninstalling the app does not cancel the subscription.

On an iPhone, open Settings, tap your name, tap Subscriptions, tap the subscription and tap Cancel Subscription. Apple says that if you started a free trial and do not want to renew, you should cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends. If there is no Cancel button, or you see an expiry message in red text, the subscription is already cancelled.

sections.heading: How tracking renewals in Essara helps
paragraphs: Once you know the yearly cost, the harder part is remembering when the charge will come. Essara is a manual tracker: you add each subscription and choose a monthly, quarterly or yearly cycle, and it shows the cost per month and per year along with the upcoming renewals. You enter these details yourself, because Essara does not connect to your bank account or UPI app.

faqs.q: Is a yearly subscription always cheaper?
faqs.a: No. A yearly plan is cheaper only if you keep the service for long enough to make up the saving. In the example above, the monthly plan is cheaper for any stay of up to 10 months, and the yearly plan wins from 11 months onwards.

faqs.q: How do I convert a quarterly or weekly price to a yearly cost?
faqs.a: Multiply a quarterly price by 4 and a weekly price by 52. For example, ₹549 a quarter is ₹2,196 a year, and ₹50 a week is ₹2,600 a year.

faqs.q: Can I get a refund for the unused months of a yearly plan?
faqs.a: Sometimes, but it depends on the seller's policy. Google's refund help page describes partial refunds for subscriptions as a region-specific policy covering Israel, France and Germany. Check the app developer's refund terms and contact them directly.

faqs.q: Does cancelling a yearly plan stop the next charge?
faqs.a: Cancelling stops the next renewal, and Google says you can keep using a subscription for the time you have already paid. On an iPhone, cancel under Settings, then Subscriptions. If the Cancel button has gone or you see an expiry message, the subscription is already cancelled.

faqs.q: Should I switch from monthly to yearly to save money?
faqs.a: Only if you are confident you will keep the service for the full year. If there is a real chance you will stop within the first 10 months, the monthly plan is the cheaper choice in the example above.
